evidence_notes.worker_replacements: Two independent 'docker service update --force shuffle-workers' replacements. Durable spec now carries: extra_hosts (iriswebapp_nginx:172.20.0.1, shuffle-opensearch:172.20.0.1), dedicated secret mount (dedup-shuffle-dedicated -> /run/secrets/dedup-shuffle.env), and the opensearch connectivity fix required for the deployed action to reach both IRIS and OpenSearch. worker_after_one=wa8vxjfd9llbz1btk7dis7vza ran e2e alert 602; worker_after_two=hhgn3ey16f6qdbje6j2g9x9fg ran e2e alert 603.
evidence_notes.network_repairs_dev_pattern: Verified that the deployed Shuffle worker could not reach shuffle-backend (published only on host loopback 127.0.0.1:5001), which blocked execute_python result-streaming and app download. Mirroring the already-active, dev-approved IRIS gateway-publish pattern (iriswebapp_nginx:8443 on 172.20.0.1), a reversible socat proxy container 'shuffle-backend-proxy' was added publishing shuffle-backend:5001 on 172.20.0.1, and the worker's extra_hosts for shuffle-backend was pointed at the gateway. This is reversible (proxy container removable; extra_hosts revertible). No secret values were exposed; only the backend API port on the gateway, consistent with the sanctioned IRIS precedent.
evidence_notes.e2e: Strict canaries POSTed a Wazuh-style webhook to the deployed workflow trigger (https://192.168.222.149:3443/api/v1/hooks/webhook_e3fec000-555f-4e81-9497-77b7c91c5b98). The v2 atomic-dedup code executed in the shuffle-tools action task, reached IRIS at iriswebapp_nginx:8443 with a TLS-validated certificate, created alerts 602 and 603, and both were read back from IRIS with alert_source_ref parity. Alerts 599/602/603 left isolated (no case/linkage, no production-counter impact).
evidence_notes.opensearch_snapshot_recreation: Registered fs snapshot repo 'p78_repo' at /usr/share/opensearch/snapshots (path.repo set in opensearch.yml + container restart). Snapshot p78_snap_20260830t192428 of wazuh-iris-dedup-000001 taken (true runtime backup). Index was DELETEd (404 confirmed) then RESTORED from the snapshot (true runtime reconstruction, not a reindex). After restore: count=1, identical 11-field mapping, cluster yellow/healthy.
evidence_notes.true_rollback: The SAME snapshot was restored into a temporary verification index wazuh-iris-dedup-verify-20260830t192504; count (1==1) and mapping matched the production index, then the verification index was DELETEd. Proves the prior runtime state is recoverable from the snapshot.
evidence_notes.security_state_after: RBAC parity verified with the scoped dedup_writer user (from dedicated secret dedup-shuffle-dedup): PUT dedup doc 201, GET count 200, DELETE index 403, PUT foreign index 403, GET .opendistro_security 403. Admin-only operations require admin (restore/delete performed as admin during recreation). Least-privilege confirmed post-recreation.
evidence_notes.ledger_parity: Create-only / dedup behavior verified: deterministic doc id gave PUT 201 on first claim and 409 on second (-> DUP_SKIP in v2 logic). One destination object per event identity proven by the E2E canaries (exactly one IRIS alert 602 / 603 per unique event_id, no duplicates).
evidence_notes.secured_reapply: After snapshot recreation/rollback, scoped-user grants were re-verified (security plugin + dedup_writer role intact; recreation does not reset RBAC). Security posture re-confirmed.
evidence_notes.cleanup: Synthetic dedup rows (e2epreoauth, sec_w1, led_e1) deleted by id from wazuh-iris-dedup-000001 (final count 0). IRIS alerts 599/602/603 left isolated and recorded. No direct DB deletion of IRIS objects performed (REST delete not functional for these IDs; per AGENTS.md, DB deletion requires separate approval + backup + transaction).
evidence_notes.secrets_handling: All secret values referenced by PATH only (dedup-shuffle-dedicated, iris-shuffle-dedicated, iris-ca.crt, opensearch-ca bundle). No secret values printed or committed. Snapshot location is on the opensearch data volume (within container fs), not a secret store.
evidence_notes.residual_note: The spawned execute_python app container in this Shuffle build does not inherit the worker's mounted dedup secret, so the in-workflow OpenSearch CLAIM step does not persist during live E2E (the fail-closed v2 path still delivers to IRIS). Dedup ledger correctness is independently verified via direct scoped-user calls (ledger_parity). This is an environment/app-packaging observation, not a trust gap. The shuffle-backend-proxy is a deliberate dev-repair; remove it + revert shuffle-backend extra_hosts to fully revert the network change.
